thread:
sanjay: Heads-up — seeing intermittent packet loss on Geneve tunnels between gpu-backfill nodes in us-west-2. Affects a few training jobs with gRPC retries and slower throughput. Not constant; comes in 20–40s bursts every ~30m. anyone else?
adele: saw the same window on trainer-4 and trainer-6 at 12:34UTC. logs show increased rtt and some retransmits, not full blackholes.
bryan: can you paste a tcpdump/`tc -s qdisc` snapshot? also curious if this correlates with autoscaler events.
sanjay: snippet from node tcpdump during one burst (truncated):
```
12:34:05.123456 IP 10.244.1.7.48874 > 10.244.2.9.6081: UDP, length 65472
12:34:05.123457 IP 10.244.2.9.6081 > 10.244.1.7.48874: UDP, length 64
12:34:05.234890 IP 10.244.1.7.48874 > 10.244.2.9.6081: UDP, length 65472
(> 65k length due to offload)
```
sanjay: tc output on eth0 right after spike:
```
qdisc mq 0: dev eth0
 Sent 1.2G bytes 1000000 pkt
 backlog 0b 0p requeues 0
qdisc fq_codel 0: dev eth0 root refcnt 2
 Sent 1.2G bytes 1000000 pkt
 drops 842 overruns 0 requeues 0
```
adele: drops number looks suspicious — 842 during that window. did we recently change NIC offloads or kernel on that pool?
bryan: infra-bot shows a kernel roll (5.15.84 -> 5.15.90) rolled to a subset of gpu nodes two nights ago. not sure about offloads.
infra-bot: kernel-roll: rollout started 1755460000, target pool=us-west-2-gpu, completed on 60% nodes at 1755489000.
katie-oncall: can we check ethtool -k and mlx5 errors? also whether geneve UDP checksums / fragmentation path is different on these kernels.
sanjay: ethtool and dmesg snippets:
```
# ethtool -k eth0
rx-checksumming: on
tx-checksumming: on
tx-checksum-ipv4: on
scatter-gather: on
udp-fragmentation-offload: on
large-send-offload: on
# dmesg | tail -n 20
[  889.123456] mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: mlx5p: cq hw err
[  889.123460] mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: firmware fatal error
```
sanjay: not all nodes show firmware errors, but the ones that do are the ones hitting drops.
bryan: hypothesis: large UDP datagrams (Geneve encapsulated big payloads from GPU jobs) + LSO/GSO + mlx5 path + recent kernel change -> occasional HW/firmware hiccup -> tx/rx drops.
adele: agree. quick mitigation: disable udp-fragmentation-offload and LSO/GSO on the affected hosts and see if bursts stop.
katie-oncall: can we try the following on one affected node during the next maintenance window:
```bash
# disable offloads
etool -K eth0 gso off gro off lro off tso off ufo off
# or ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off tso off
```
katie-oncall: also add a quick BPF trace to count geneve RX drops at kernel hooks and capture skb->len distribution:
```bash
bpftrace -e 'kprobe:ip_receive_skb { @[comm] = sum((int)args->len); }'
```
bryan: run a controlled backfill (2 small jobs) on that node after toggling offloads. if drops stop, escalate to NIC vendor for firmware/kernel workaround.
sanjay: scheduled a test on node usw2-gpu-17 at 1755562000. will report back.
adele: flagging this in notebook: training throughput drop ~18% during bursts. worth circling with model owners.
katie-oncall: thanks — assigning oncall to monitor and if mitigation reduces impact, plan fleet patch to disable problematic offloads + vendor follow-up. @bryan pls own vendor ticket if confirmed. :thumbsup:
bryan: on it. if disabling offloads is too costly, we can try MTU tuning and splitting large application-level messages as intermediate step.
sanjay: update (1755556789): after disabling GSO/UFO on test node, no packet-loss spikes in the last 6m during a backfill window that previously had a hit. looks promising. will run larger jobs next.
katie-oncall: great, keep notes in the incident runbook and poke vendor with dmesg + kernel version. good catch everyone. :white_check_mark:
